newsitem.title: USA: New Year's celebration a nightmare for Texas father.
newsitem.headline: New Year's celebration a nightmare for Texas father.

text.p: A grieving father told reporters on Thursday of how a New Year's celebration became a parent's worst nightmare when he accidentally shot his daughter to death.

Randy Farmer, 34, was charged with criminally negligent homicide in the killing of 7-year-old Mary Farmer, but he said no legal action or jail sentence could be worse than the tragedy that had already happened.

"Everybody who knows her knows that my daughter was just the sweetest little angel there is. And these courts, they can't do the damage to me I've done to myself," he said, weeping almost uncontrollably as he stood outside the courtroom of state district judge Mary Lou Keel.
"I've lost everything. She was my everything," Farmer said.

Farmer said he went outside of his house at midnight on Tuesday to fire off his pistol to celebrate the arrival of 1997. The gun jammed, so he went back inside, where his daughter was lying on a couch, to try to remove the bullet.

"I was trying to get the bullet out and she (Mary) stood up and said 'Daddy' and the gun went off. She hit the floor and rolled over and she just looked up at me and said, 'Daddy, I'm OK'," Farmer said.
"I said, 'no, you're not, lay there.' I said everything will be OK, just stay there and lay there, but after that she just died. And I'm so sorry," he said.
Farmer attempted to resuscitate his daugther, who was struck in the chest, but it was too late.
"It was an accidental shooting. God gave her to me -- I was the first to hold her when she was born, I was the last one to hold her when she died," he said, wiping away tears.

Farmer was released from jail after posting a $2,000 bond. He told Judge Keel on Thursday that he did not have enough money to pay for a lawyer, but she did not grant his request for a court-appointed attorney and set Jan. 24 as the day for his arraignment.
If convicted, Farmer could face up to 10 years in jail.
Funeral services for Mary Farmer were set for Saturday, the family said. Farmer and his wife also have two sons.
